questions.help:
9 The negative effects of speed
 
Through the driver’s vision, 90% of the information needed for good driving is received: the condition and configuration of the road, signalling, distances, speeds etc. Hence, the importance of having the largest possible zone of vision when driving. Speed, among other factors, causes a decrease in the useful field of vision, which results in a tunnel vision effect. Therefore, as speed increases the driver’s field of vision is reduced eventually resulting in only objects in the centre of the roadway being clearly visible. The peripheral vision is steadily reduced as speed increases also.
 
(Página 178 del manual 'Learning to drive')

12 Wheels and tyres
12.1 Maintenance
Check the tyre pressures using a properly approved and tested tyre gauge at least once or twice a month. These can be found at public and private locations.

(Página 245 del manual 'Learning to drive')

6. Groups of drivers most at risk of a collision
6.1 The young
6.1.1 The primary cause of juvenile mortality 
Young drivers generally have a number of advantages over the remainder of drivers, as generally they are in a better condition of physical fitness, have better reflexes and skills that are more suited to driving. However, these favourable conditions do not help if the driver is not aware of his limitations, including lack of experience or the tendency to take more risks.
There are many young people who drive safely and therefore have no increased risk of being involved in a collision than other older drivers.
However, in Spain each year hundreds of young people die in road traffic collisions, which are the leading cause of death in the 15 to 29 year age group. Therefore the problem of road collisions is even more worrying for young people in this age group than for others outside it.
 
(Página 253 del manual 'Learning to drive')

12.3 The stopping distance
The overall stopping distance is the distance the vehicle takes to come to a complete stop from the point at which the driver first sees the hazard to the point the vehicle comes to a final stop. In other words it is the result of adding the reaction distance and the braking distance together.

questions.help:
Priorities, level crossings and tunnels      
     
5 Narrow Sections  
5.2 Narrowing section without signed priority
5.2.1 Order of preference in the absence of road signs
The following explains the order of preference in the absence of road signs, signals or authorised persons, and applies to priority when different types of vehicles approach a narrow road section and it is necessary for one of the vehicles to reverse back to allow the other vehicle to pass. Under these circumstance priority is given as follows:
1.Special vehicles and those travelling under special regulations that exceed the established masses and dimensions as per the regulated rules of vehicles (MAM).
2. Set of vehicles-except those within point 4 below.
3. Vehicles pulled by animals.
4. Cars that tow a trailer of up to 750 kilograms MAM and camping vehicles.
5.Public transport vehicles-designed to transport passengers.
6. Lorries, tractive units and good vans and goods vehicles.
7. Car and vehicles derived from cars.
8. Special vehicles that do not exceed the mass or dimension established within the regulating laws; heavy quadricycles and light quadricycles.
9. Three wheeled vehicles, motorcycles with sidecar and three wheeled mopeds.
10. Motorcycles, two wheeled mopeds and bicycles.
(Página 209 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Maneouvres  
 
2 Safety rules M.S.M.
2.2 Signal: Advising and warning of the manoeuvre
All sideways movements, change of direction or ‘U’ turns must be warned of by the following means:
Using the directional indicator (lighting signal) that corresponds to the direction that the vehicle will be turning, or
With the arm horizontally extended and the palm of the hand indicating that the movement (change of course) is towards the side shown –i.e. left (for a left hand drive car –this is the correct method of indicating a movement to the left).
With the arm horizontally extended and bent upwards, and with the palm of the hand facing upwards and indicating that the movement (change of course) is to the opposite side –normally to the right. (Again this is normal practise for a left hand drive car / motor vehicle).
(Página 183 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES    
   
3 Brakes
3.5 Improvements in braking systems
3.5.1 Anti-lock braking system (ABS)
ABS is an important advancement in the field of active vehicle safety, since:
It allows the driver to maintain control over the steering. (If the wheels are locked the vehicle will not respond to the way the driver turns the steering wheel).
In most cases, ABS reduces the braking distance for the average driver.
The effectiveness of ABS is limited by the capacity of the adhesion of the tyres to the road surface. Defective tyres or shock absorbers will reduce the effectiveness of ABS and will extend the braking length.
(Página 65 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
9 Hard shoulders  
 
On some roadways there is an area that runs parallel to the main carriageway, this is called the ‘hard shoulder.’
The following must travel on the hard shoulder, on the right going with the traffic flow, (unless there is a road or part of it specifically designated for their use:
Vehicles pulled by animals.
Special vehicles with a MAM not exceeding 3,500 kg’.
Cycles.
Vehicles following cyclists.
Mopeds.
Vehicles for people with reduced mobility.
However the hard shoulder must be useable. When the road does not have a hard shoulder or it is not useable or sufficient, for instance it is not wide enough, these users must travel as close as possible to the right edge of the roadway, occupying as little as possible of the roadway.
(Página 168 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
21 Audible warning instrument - horn
 
The horn can only be used in certain circumstances, as a warning to:
Avoid a possible accident; such as in narrow roads, hump back bridges or roads with bends with little or no visibility.
To warn, on roads outside of a built-up-area, that the vehicle behind is overtaking or planning to do so.
To warn other road users, that the vehicle is being used as a highpriority vehicle –normally reserved for emergency service vehicles.
(Página 106 del manual 'Learning to drive')
